primitives.name: Isotonic Calibration Rejection
primitives.verbatim_quote: What: NFL win-probability model with a real held-out **2025 test: Brier .1613, log loss .4831, AUC .8459, ECE .0331** (DIRECT) — tested isotonic calibration and **rejected it when it worsened the holdout**.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes a proper scoring rule (Brier score, log loss) as the loss function \mathcal{L}. Requires an independent holdout set for evaluation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Overfitting regime where calibration introduces bias that outweighs variance reduction, leading to worse out-of-sample performance.

layer2.mapping: Dual to GSI's conformal prediction rejection when nonconformity scores are poorly distributed. Both reject based on out-of-sample predictive sharpness.
layer2.telemetry: Holdout log-loss difference; e.g., GSI tracks daily \(\Delta \mathcal{L} = \mathcal{L}_{\text{conformal}} - \mathcal{L}_{\text{base}}\)

primitives.name: Walk-Forward Validation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Fit: validation ritual against the closing line is exactly GSE's honesty standard; the walk-forward design is worth copying wholesale.
primitives.assumptions: Time-series stationarity, \(X_t \perp Y_{t+h}|X_{\le t}\) for \(h>1\); requires independent test distribution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Static distribution shift where future data differs from training/test splits, causing systematic bias in validation metrics.

layer2.mapping: Equivalence to GSE's state-transition testing, where each forward step updates the model state \(\theta_t\) using only information available at time \(t\).
layer2.telemetry: Validation accuracy on closing-line-adjusted predictions; e.g., GSE tracks rolling 5-game win-rate

primitives.name: Monte Carlo Simulation
primitives.verbatim_quote: What: **SOS-adjusted offensive/defensive ratings, 12-game trailing window, Bayesian prior-season blending, hypothesis-tested ~10% home-field advantage, generalized Poisson for under-dispersed TD counts, separate rare-event distributions, 5,000-run Monte Carlo in Excel, Power Query automation** (all DIRECT from channel content).
primitives.assumptions: iid samples from the underlying distribution \(P(X)\); high-dimensional integration via sampling.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Convergence rate \(O(N^{-1/2})\) becomes prohibitive for high-precision tasks; variance reduction techniques may be needed.

layer2.mapping: Generalizes GSE's probabilistic state transitions, where each transition is simulated stochastically to estimate outcome distributions.
layer2.telemetry: Simulation variance; e.g., GSE monitors standard error of estimated win probabilities

primitives.name: Rare Event Distributions
primitives.verbatim_quote: What: **SOS-adjusted offensive/defensive ratings, 12-game trailing window, Bayesian prior-season blending, hypothesis-tested ~10% home-field advantage, generalized Poisson for under-dispersed TD counts, separate rare-event distributions, 5,000-run Monte Carlo in Excel, Power Query automation** (all DIRECT from channel content).
primitives.assumptions: Event \(A\) has low base rate; tail behavior can be approximated by extreme value theory or compound Poisson processes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: High false-positive rates in classification; requires specialized metrics like precision at k or normalized discounted cumulative gain.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's tail-risk quantile estimation, where standard models fail and bespoke distributions are fitted to the extremal data.
layer2.telemetry: Rare-event detection rate; e.g., GSI tracks false-alarm ratio on high-odds bets
